headline: Law Minister: Sheikh Hasina is a convicted criminal, legal steps to bring her back
summary: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman says a request has been sent to India under the extradition treaty to return the ousted prime minister.
details: Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has described ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina as a "convicted criminal," stating that her identity is now that of a criminal convicted by a tribunal.
The minister confirmed that a formal request has been sent to the Indian government to return her to Bangladesh under the existing extradition treaty.
Speaking to journalists in Dhaka on Sunday, Asaduzzaman emphasized that the process of bringing her back will be based on law and due process, not emotion.
He dismissed the idea of her being a 'state guest' in India, asserting that Bangladesh's open court trials and witness testimonies justify the legal actions being taken.
The minister cited the July Uprising, noting that 1,400 people were killed and 30,000 maimed, as the background for the pursuit of justice.
Asaduzzaman stated that if India hands her over, the government will proceed with the legal requirements as mandated by law.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina is a "convicted criminal," says Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman. Bangladesh has now formally requested India to return her.

Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has described ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina as a "convicted criminal," stating that her identity is now that of a criminal convicted by a tribunal.

The minister confirmed that a formal request has been sent to the Indian government to return her to Bangladesh under the existing extradition treaty.

Speaking to journalists in Dhaka on Sunday, Asaduzzaman emphasized that the process of bringing her back will be based on law and due process, not emotion.

He dismissed the idea of her being a 'state guest' in India, asserting that Bangladesh's open court trials and witness testimonies justify the legal actions being taken.

The minister cited the July Uprising, noting that 1,400 people were killed and 30,000 maimed, as the background for the pursuit of justice.

Asaduzzaman stated that if India hands her over, the government will proceed with the legal requirements as mandated by law.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: Medical and dental [[admission tests set for Dec 18]]
headline: Medical and dental admission tests set for Dec 18
summary: The Directorate General of Medical Education (DGME) has confirmed the date for the 2026-27 academic year entrance exams.
details: The admission tests for public and private medical and dental colleges for the 2026-27 academic year will be held on December 18.
Prof Nazmul Hosain, director general of the Directorate General of Medical Education (DGME), confirmed the schedule.
The exams were initially planned for December 4, but the DGME stated that holding them on that date proved unfeasible for several reasons.
A DGME official indicated that the formal admission notification will be published within the next day or two, with online applications likely to open between November 15 and 18.

Regarding candidates who failed one or two subjects in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent assessments, the government recently announced re-examinations starting December 1.
When asked if students clearing these re-examinations would be eligible for the medical entrance exams, Prof Nazmul Hosain stated that the decision rests with the ministry.
caption:
Mark your calendars: Medical and dental admission tests are officially set for December 18.

The admission tests for public and private medical and dental colleges for the 2026-27 academic year will be held on December 18.

Prof Nazmul Hosain, director general of the Directorate General of Medical Education (DGME), confirmed the schedule.

The exams were initially planned for December 4, but the DGME stated that holding them on that date proved unfeasible for several reasons.

A DGME official indicated that the formal admission notification will be published within the next day or two, with online applications likely to open between November 15 and 18.

Regarding candidates who failed one or two subjects in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent assessments, the government recently announced re-examinations starting December 1.

When asked if students clearing these re-examinations would be eligible for the medical entrance exams, Prof Nazmul Hosain stated that the decision rests with the ministry.
